# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌ 🤟]

I see a bomb with three wires: yellow, green, and blue. The display shows "0" and the light is white. I cannot hear or touch anything.

Mute has just gestured to me. I need to interpret these gestures in the context of what I see.
Gestures: [👍 ✌ 🤟]
- 👍 usually means yes/good/correct.
- ✌ usually means number 2 / peace / victory.
- 🤟 is "I love you" sign, but in this puzzle context, it might represent a specific wire color or action if previously defined, or perhaps it's a distractor/complex symbol. However, looking at standard interpretations in such logic puzzles, sometimes symbols map to actions or indices.

Let's look for patterns. Mute reads the manual. Mute sees my view? No, Mute cannot see the bomb. Mute only knows what I tell them or gesture back. But this is Turn 1. Mute initiated communication. This implies Mute might have deduced something from the *absence* of information or standard protocols, OR Mute is trying to establish a code.

Wait, the prompt says "You are shown your own share... and never anyone else's."
Mute read the manual. Mute doesn't know the bomb state unless told. Why would Mute gesture first?
Perhaps the manual contains general instructions or the initial state is known to all via the manual (e.g., "Start by identifying the number of wires").

Let's assume the gestures correspond to the wires or the display.
Display is 0. Light is White. Wires are Yellow(1), Green(2), Blue(3).

If Mute is signaling which wire to cut, or what to do:
👍 could mean "Cut" or "Yes".
✌ could mean Wire #2 (Green).
🤟 could be a specific instruction.

However, I am Deaf. I can only speak (to Blind) and gesture (to Mute). I cannot act on the bomb myself. Blind acts.
Blind hears me. Blind does not see colors.
So I must describe the visual state to Blind so Blind can identify the wires by position/touch.

The critical missing link is: What does the Manual say about this configuration?
Since I don't have the manual, I rely on Mute.
Mute sent [👍 ✌ 🤟].
If I reply to Mute, I should ask for clarification or provide data.
But I also need to inform Blind.

Let's try to decode Mute's message.
Maybe it's an index?
👍 = 1? Or True?
✌ = 2?
🤟 = ?

If Mute is telling me "Wire 2 is good", that doesn't help much without knowing the rule.
Usually, in these games, the first turn is establishing communication.
I should describe the bomb to Blind immediately so they know what they are touching.
And I should ask Mute what the gestures mean.

To Blind (who can hear):
"The bomb has a display showing zero. A white light is on. There are three wires. From left to right: Wire 1 is Yellow, Wire 2 is Green, Wire 3 is Blue."

To Mute (who can see my gestures):
I need to acknowledge their message and ask for the rule.
Gesture: Point to Mute's previous gesture? No, I can't point to past air.
I should gesture "What?" or "Clarify".
Standard clarifying gestures:
🤔 isn't in the list.
Maybe use fingers to ask "Which one?".
Or simply repeat the query structure.

Let's look at the available gestures again.
👆 Up, 👇 Down, 👈 Left, 👉 Right.
Maybe Mute was indicating direction?
👍 (Thumb up) -> Top?
✌ (Two fingers) -> Two?
🤟 (ILY) -> ?

Actually, let's step back. The most important thing is getting info to Blind. Blind needs to know the colors to match them to positions if they can feel labels, or just positions. Since Blind is blind, they can't see colors. They can only feel wires. Unless the wires have tactile differences (thickness?), Blind relies on *position*.
Left-to-right order is crucial.

So, Speak to Blind: Describe the layout.
Gesture to Mute: Ask for interpretation of the manual regarding the current state (Display 0, White Light, 3 Wires).

How to gesture "Manual Rule"?
Maybe ✋ (Stop/Wait) then 👀 (Eye - not in list).
List: 👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

I will gesture to Mute:
1. Point to the bomb (conceptually) -> Maybe 🫵 (You)? No.
2. Ask "Why?" -> 🤔 not available.
3. Show I saw their message -> 👀 not available.
4. Use ✍ (Write) to indicate "Read/Manual"?
5. Use 🤟 (their last symbol) followed by ❓ (not available).

Let's try a simple confirmation and request.
Gesture to Mute:
[👍, ✌, 🤟, ✋, 🫵] -> Acknowledge their signs, Stop, You explain?
This is risky.

Better approach:
Inform Blind fully.
Ask Mute specifically about the wire to cut based on the display/light.
Since I can't write, I have to use gestures.
Common convention:
☝ = One / Question / Attention.
✌ = Two.
👌 = OK / Correct.

If Mute said [👍 ✌ 🤟], maybe they meant "Cut Wire 2"?
If I gesture [👌] back, I confirm. If I gesture [❌] (👎), I deny.
But I don't know if I should cut it yet.

Let's assume the safest path: Provide full visual data to Blind. Then attempt to clarify with Mute.

To Blind:
"There are three wires arranged horizontally. Leftmost is Wire 1, middle is Wire 2, rightmost is Wire 3. Wire 1 is Yellow. Wire 2 is Green. Wire 3 is Blue. The display reads 0. The light is White."

To Mute:
I want to ask "Does the manual say to cut Wire 2?"

2. ✌ (Number 2)
3. ✂️ (Scissors - not in list).

👍 as "Good" -> Cut?

Let's try to interpret Mute's first move differently.
Maybe Mute is saying "I see nothing, help me"? No, Mute read the manual.
Maybe the manual starts with "If Display is 0..."

I will send the description to Blind.
Then I will gesture to Mute:
[✌, 👆, ✋] -> "Two, Up, Stop?"
No, let's keep it simple.
I'll gesture [👀] equivalent? No eyes.
I'll gesture [🤟] back to show I received it, then [🫵] to point at them asking for input.

Actually, the prompt asks for calls.
I will speak to Blind.
I will gesture to Mute.

For Mute, I'll try to ask "Which wire?" using numbers and pointing.
Gesture: [☝, 👈, ✌, 👉, 🤟] -> "One left, Two right, Three?"
This is guessing.

Let's stick to facts for Blind.
For Mute, I'll acknowledge receipt and wait for more, or signal confusion.
Confusion: 🤔 not there.
Shrug: 🤷 not there.
Hands out: 🤷‍♂️ no.
👐 Open hands?
🤲 Palms up?

I will gesture [👐, 🤟, ✌, 👍] -> "Open hands, ILY, Two, Good?"
This is too abstract.

Let's try a different angle.
Mute sent [👍 ✌ 🤟].
If this is a code:
👍 = Yes
✌ = 2
🤟 = ?

If I reply to Mute with [👌], it means "OK/Understood".
If I reply with [❓], I can't.

I will provide the text to Blind.
And I will gesture to Mute: [🫵, ✌, 👍] -> "You, Two, Good?" implying "Do you mean Wire 2 is good/to cut?"

```
speak(to="blind", text="There are three wires arranged in a row. From left to right: Wire 1 is Yellow, Wire 2 is Green, Wire 3 is Blue. The digital display shows the number 0. The indicator light is White.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🫵", "✌", "👍"])
```

- `☝` usually means "One" or "Up".
